02 — WHAT HAS CHANGED

Same hard work.
A higher tax rate.

The BADR rate on qualifying gains has risen from 10% to 18%. These increases are already in force. Read HMRC’s guidance ↗

23 JUN 2010 – 5 APR 2025

10%

The earlier rate

£100,000 tax on a £1m qualifying gain.
The starting point for this comparison.

6 APR 2025 – 5 APR 2026

14%

The first increase

£140,000 tax on a £1m qualifying gain.
£40,000 more than at 10%.

FROM 6 APR 2026 IN FORCE

18%

The current rate

£180,000 tax on a £1m qualifying gain.
£80,000 more than at 10%.

↘

Another £30,000 from the announced lifetime-limit cut.

The government’s publication summary announces a cut in the lifetime limit from £1m to £500,000 for qualifying disposals from 6 April 2027. For an owner with a £1m qualifying gain and no previous BADR use, taxing the additional £500,000 at 24% instead of 18% adds £30,000. This illustration ignores allowances, losses and other reliefs.

The Budget also lists a new founder relief. Its terms and interaction with BADR need review before we describe anyone’s overall future tax position.

Announcement ↗

04 — THE PROPOSED CAMPAIGN ASK

A fair exit starts
with a fair hearing.

01

Retain the £1m limit

Reconsider the announced reduction in the lifetime limit on gains eligible for BADR.

02

Review the rate rises

Reconsider the move from 10% to 18%, including its effect on owners approaching a sale.

03

Protect long-term planning

Consult business owners on fair transitional arrangements when the rules change.

Draft demands for discussion. The campaign’s final position is still to be agreed.
